findings.reason: The two standalone original-resolution tiles contain a complete analytic argument but no illustration. A marked source fibre and its opposite local signs make the essential distinction between unsigned cardinality and signed degree visible. A separate target image arc prevents the misleading impression that the map is surjective. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a failure of the rigorous proof.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section containing a signed-fibre TikZ schematic, counterclockwise orientation arrows, image arc and the two counts.

correction: Added an explanatory diagram only; all original bytes are an unchanged prefix, including the complete statement, Facts, proof, sources, dependency list and published status.

diagram_math_checks.objects_and_map: Source and target are the counterclockwise oriented circles S^1 from Given; F(e^{i theta})=e^{i sin theta} maps source to target, exactly as the Statement and step 1.1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The sole horizontal arrow denotes this whole map, not a bijection or a path between selected points.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The marked right source point theta=0 and left source point theta=pi both map to target 1 and are exactly F^{-1}(1).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2.1 solves sin(theta) in 2 pi Z, uses |sin(theta)|<=1<2 pi, and lists precisely the quotient classes 0 and 1/2.

diagram_math_checks.orientation_and_signs: Both circle orientation arrows increase polar angle counterclockwise. The right source point is labelled +1 and left source point -1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Given fixes both orientations. F3 and steps 1.1–2.1 give angular derivative cos(theta), equal to +1 at 0 and -1 at pi.
The two marked points are regular by their nonzero derivatives, and F5 / step 2.1 supplies the signed regular-fibre formula.

diagram_math_checks.image_arc: The thick target arc spans angles -1 to 1 radians, displayed approximately as -57.2958 to 57.2958 degrees on the right side of the target circle; the remainder remains thin.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The existing formula has phase sin(theta), bounded by 1 in absolute value by F2. Sine attains -1 and +1 at the quarter-turn values in F3 and is continuous by its differentiability, so its range is exactly [-1,1]. This is a proper arc, consistent with the omitted target fibre in step 3.1.
